analysis.title: Veralto Corp. (VLTO): Healthy demand drives 3Q26 beat; FY2026 outlook raised with growth accelerating into 4Q; Buy
key_insights: VLTO reported 3Q26 revenue of $1.51bn, modestly above GSe and FactSet consensus of $1.50bn, with total sales growth of 7.5%.
Core sales growth of 5.1% exceeded GSe of 4.4%. Water Quality revenue of $939mn (vs. GSe ~$916mn) grew 6.4% organically. PQI revenue of $570mn (vs. GSe $579mn) grew 3.2% organically.
Adj. operating margin expanded 170bps yoy to 25.6%, ahead of GSe of 24.2%. Water Quality and PQI adj. operating margins were 26.6% and 28.2%, up 30bps and 280bps yoy.
Adj. EBITDA of $397mn exceeded GSe/consensus of $373mn/$374mn. Adj. EPS of $1.18 exceeded GSe/consensus of $1.08/$1.09.

4Q26 core sales growth guided to +5.5%-6.5% (GSe 6.4%), an acceleration from +5.1% in 3Q26. Management expects PQI growth to accelerate further in 4Q, supported by digital workflow, steady Marking & Coding demand and improvement in color measurement.

FY26 guidance raised: core sales growth to +4.2%-4.5% (from +4.0%-4.5%), adj. operating margin expansion to ~50bps (from +25-50bps), and adj. EPS to $4.49-$4.52 (from $4.35-$4.43), above GSe/consensus of $4.37/$4.39.

Cost optimization benefits are arriving earlier than expected. VLTO now expects $10-$15mn of savings in FY2026. About half of the targeted $65-$75mn annual savings is expected in 2027, with full run-rate in 2028.

4Q margin guidance is ~24.5% adj. operating margin: ~30bps from underlying fall-through (30%-35%) and ~40bps from cost optimization, offset by dilution from the recently completed Cleanwater1 acquisition.

Sales supporting data center investments within Water Quality more than doubled in 3Q. Management calls the opportunity relatively small today but predominantly recurring once data centers become operational. GS sees a longer-duration growth opportunity in industrial water treatment.

Capital deployment: $1.1bn across four bolt-on acquisitions YTD (In-Situ, GlobalVision, Alfaa UV, Cleanwater1) and $550mn of share repurchases, equal to 2.4% of shares outstanding. Management cites an active acquisition pipeline.
GS adj. EBITDA estimates for 2026E-2028E rose 1%/4%/4% to $1.53bn/$1.66bn/$1.76bn. GS 2026E adj. EPS rose to $4.51 from $4.37.

GS raised its 12-month price target to $132 from $118 (18.8% upside from $111.10). The SOTP uses 20X EV/EBITDA for Water Quality (from 19X) and 19X for Product Quality & Innovation (from 18X) on Q5-Q8 EBITDA.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised to $132 from $118 after a 3Q26 beat and a raised FY26 outlook, with higher EV/EBITDA multiples on both segments.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue reported $1.51bn vs GSe and FactSet consensus est $1.50bn, reported 10/30, total growth 7.5%, core growth 5.1% vs GSe 4.4%.
3Q26 adj. EPS reported $1.18 vs GSe $1.08 and consensus est $1.09. GAAP EPS (basic) reported $1.04 vs GSe $1.01.
3Q26 adj. EBITDA reported $397mn vs GSe $373mn and consensus est $374mn. Adj. operating margin reported 25.6% vs GSe 24.2%.
FY2026 adj. EPS guidance raised to $4.49-$4.52 from $4.35-$4.43, vs GSe $4.37 and consensus est $4.39 before the update. GS now models FY26E adj. EPS of $4.51, FY27E $4.63, FY28E $5.01.
4Q26 guidance: core sales growth +5.5%-6.5% and adj. operating margin of ~24.5%. GSe core growth is 6.4%.
3Q26 tax rate was 7% reported vs GS estimate of 20%, which helped non-GAAP net income of $290mn vs GSe $263.9mn.
risk_factors: Slower rebound in consumer CPG/HPC/Pharma demand.
Lack of global expansion and industrial spend.
Near-term margin dilution from acquisitions, including Cleanwater1.
